## Summary

First vertical slice of the G8 resource HUD: a reusable `ResourceHud` component in `src/ui/` that renders a **caller-declared** resource set as one labelled item per key, in declaration order, exported from the `@ui` barrel. This slice covers the declared-set rendering contract only; bounds/irreversible markers (child 2) and the update path (child 3) follow.

## Target outcome

A scene developer can construct `new ResourceHud(scene, { x, y, align, declaredKeys, resources, labels })` at an SLL-resolved point and see exactly one labelled item per declared key, in declaration order, with the current value — with no resource key, label, order or value hard-coded in the component.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A reusable resource-HUD component (`ResourceHud`) is exported from the `@ui` barrel (`src/ui/index.ts`) and renders a caller-declared resource set: exactly one labelled item per declared key, in declaration order, each showing the key's display label and current value, with no resource key, label, order or value hard-coded in the component.
- The component takes a plain-data options object (`{ x, y, align?, resources, declaredKeys, bounds?, irreversible?, labels?, reducedMotion?, soundManager?, sfx?, onChange?, style? }`) and `src/ui/` gains no `@story-line` import.
- The component supports left / centre / right alignment around the SLL anchor point, so a right-aligned `statusBar.resources` anchor renders correctly.
- A caller-supplied `labels` record overrides the display label; a key with no label prints as authored (capitalised at most), with no invented pluralisation.
- Headless unit tests (mocked Phaser, matching `tests/ui/HintBar.test.ts`) assert label, declaration order and value rendering from an arbitrary resource bag including a non-GDD key (for example `supply`, `heat`).

## Minimal implementation

1. Add `src/ui/ResourceHud.ts` extending `UIComponentBase`, with the options interface and a container of per-key label/value `Text` objects.
2. Resolve alignment from the supplied anchor (`left` / `centre` / `right`) and position each item from `x` / `y` without a literal coordinate.
3. Export `ResourceHud` and its option types from `src/ui/index.ts`; do **not** add it to `src/ui/node-safe-modules.ts`.
4. Add `tests/ui/resourceHud.test.ts` with a mocked Phaser scene; assert order, labels, values, alignment origin and an arbitrary key set (test-first inside the slice: write the assertions, then make them green before committing).

## Key Files

- `src/ui/ResourceHud.ts`
- `src/ui/index.ts`
- `tests/ui/resourceHud.test.ts`

## Dependencies

None (first slice).

## Deliverables

- `ResourceHud` declared-set render contract (labels, declaration order, values, alignment) exported from `@ui`.
- Headless unit tests for the declared-set rendering contract.

## Impact

A game developer can render any declared resource set — labels, declaration order and current values — as one aligned HUD row, so a five-key economy is legible in play without hand-rolled scene text.

data.description:
## Summary

Second vertical slice of the G8 resource HUD: bounds and the loss-bearing marker. A bounded key prints `value / max`; a key at its maximum and at its minimum each carry a printed state marker as well as a colour cue; a declared irreversible key prints `irreversible` beside it (colour is secondary), matching GDD §3.4.3.

## Target outcome

A designer's authored caps and the never-restored subset are legible in the HUD from plain data, and every state is signalled without relying on colour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A bounded key renders its declared maximum alongside the current value (for example `Morale 5 / 8`); a key at its declared maximum and a key at its declared minimum are each distinguishable by a **printed** channel as well as any colour cue.
- A key in the declared irreversible / loss-bearing subset is marked by a **printed** channel (the word `irreversible`, or an equivalent glyph with accompanying text) beside the key as well as by colour, matching the "Irreversible key" row of GDD §3.4.3.
- Bounds and irreversibility are supplied as plain data (the caller's `bounds` / `irreversible` records) and render correctly for arbitrary key sets, not only the five GDD keys.
- An unbounded key renders no `value / max`, and a key outside the irreversible subset renders no irreversible marker.
- Headless unit tests cover the `value / max` display, the at-maximum printed marker, the at-minimum printed marker and the irreversible printed + colour marker.

## Minimal implementation

1. Extend `ResourceHud` rendering with a per-key `value / max` text when `bounds[key]` exists.
2. Add printed at-maximum / at-minimum state markers plus a secondary colour tint (the printed channel is primary).
3. Add the printed `irreversible` marker beside a key in the `irreversible` set, with the §3.4.3 secondary colour cue.
4. Extend `tests/ui/resourceHud.test.ts` for max display, both printed state markers, the irreversible marker and the no-marker cases (test-first inside the slice).

## Key Files

- `src/ui/ResourceHud.ts`
- `tests/ui/resourceHud.test.ts`

## Dependencies

- Child 1 (declared-set rendering) — the markers extend the same per-key items.

## Deliverables

- Bounded-key display and printed at-maximum / at-minimum markers.
- Printed irreversible marker with a secondary colour cue.
- Headless unit tests for both.

## Impact

A player can read a capped key as "value / cap" and see, in print rather than colour alone, when a key is full, empty, or a one-way loss.

data.comment:
Slice 2 implemented (bounds + printed markers).

Changes:
- `src/ui/ResourceHud.ts`: per-key bounds read via new `readResourceBounds()` (absent/non-finite `max` = unbounded, non-finite `min` floors to 0); printed `value / max` via `formatResourceAmount()`; printed state markers via `resolveResourceState()`; printed `irreversible` marker for the caller's subset; `RESOURCE_HUD_MARKERS` pins the three marker words; `ResourceHudItem` now exposes `min`, `max`, `state`, `irreversible`, `color`.
- `src/ui/index.ts`: exports the new helpers, const and `ResourceHudState` type.
- `tests/ui/resourceHud.test.ts`: 19 new headless tests (value/max display, unbounded keys, malformed bounds, at-max/at-min printed markers, marker colour cues, irreversible printed + colour marker, arbitrary key sets/subsets, unbounded irreversible key, pure helpers). Red witness recorded before implementation (19 failures in resourceHud.test.ts only).

Decisions (documented in code):
- Marker wording `full` / `empty` per parent Q11; the GDD pins `irreversible`.
- `full` at or beyond the declared maximum and `empty` at or below the minimum (robust to an unclamped bag); between-bounds keys print neither.
- Colour is secondary: the irreversible cue takes precedence over an edge cue, and the printed word is always present.
- Values print as supplied — the HUD is a view and never silently clamps.

Gates: `npm run build` green (prebuild `check:ui-node-surface` OK, 17 modules), eslint clean on both files, changed-scope unit suite green (`/skill:test --type unit --scope changed`, 296 files / 5120 tests).

Documentation: this slice ships code comments only; the developer reference, Gym index and GDD status flip are owned by `CG-0MWZ9WD9P003IAQM` (per the parent plan), so no doc-update child is needed.

data.author: implement
data.comment:
Attribution analysis (filed from the dev-push gate of CG-0MWZ9W8VG008LUZS).

Why this is unlikely to be caused by that change:
- The change under test touched only `src/ui/ResourceHud.ts` (+197/−13), `src/ui/index.ts` (barrel exports, additive) and `tests/ui/resourceHud.test.ts`. No Gym scene, no button-bar module and no layout file was edited.
- `ResourceHud` was already exported from the `@ui` barrel by the preceding slice (commit 9389d665), so this change adds no new import edge to the Gym boot path — only extra named exports.
- The failure is **file-level** (no individual test name), which is the signature of a browser boot/collection failure rather than an assertion inside a test. `GymButtonBarVisibility.browser.test.ts` boots five Phaser games in one file, the highest-risk file for browser-context exhaustion.
- The gate run was under heavy contention: the runner reported `host load 38.4 over 16 cores` and a 250 MB `dbg.rss` dump was written at the same time (2026-11-27T20:24Z).

Suggested first diagnostic: re-run that single browser file on an idle host (Phaser 4 context exhaustion is load-sensitive), then re-run the full suite. Note the project's retry-once transient handling already ran, so a repeat failure on an idle host is a genuine regression.
